_comment: Cross-lane parity for @enforcement_effect validation. Both the Python suite (tests/test_policy_annotations.py) and the TypeScript suite (ts/test/policy-annotations.test.mjs) render these TEMPLATES and assert their own message builder produces the same string, so the two lanes cannot drift in wording. The accepted VERB LIST is deliberately not repeated here: it lives in exactly two places (src/watchlight/_annotations.py and ts/src/annotations.ts) and each lane's suite reads the other lane's source to prove they match.
error_template: {where}: @{annotation}("{value}") is not an effect this engine implements. Accepted: {accepted}. An effect the engine does not implement is dropped, and on a `permit` that turns an approval hold into an unconditional allow — so the policy is refused here rather than deciding differently from what it says.
warning_template: watchlight: {where}: `@{written}` is not an annotation Watchlight reads, and it is a near miss for `@{annotation}`. As written it is inert — the policy decides as if the effect were absent, so an approval gate would be a plain allow. Fix the spelling, or ignore this if the annotation is your own.
